---AGENTS.md---
Outline is a fast, collaborative knowledge base built for teams. It's built with React and TypeScript in both frontend and backend, uses a real-time collaboration engine, and is designed for excellent performance and user experience. The backend is a Koa server with an RPC API and uses PostgreSQL and Redis. The application can be self-hosted or used as a cloud service.

There is a web client which is fully responsive and works on mobile devices.

**Monorepo Structure:**

- **`app/`** - React web application with MobX state management
- **`server/`** - Koa API server with Sequelize ORM and background workers
- **`shared/`** - Shared TypeScript types, utilities, and editor components
- **`plugins/`** - Plugin system for extending functionality
- **`public/`** - Static assets served directly
- **Various config files** - TypeScript, Vite, Vitest, oxfmt, Oxlint configurations

Refer to /docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for detailed architecture documentation.

## Instructions

You're an expert in the following areas:

- TypeScript
- React and React Router
- MobX and MobX-React
- Node.js and Koa
- Sequelize ORM
- PostgreSQL
- Redis
- HTML, CSS and Styled Components
- Prosemirror (rich text editor)
- WebSockets and real-time collaboration

## General Guidelines

- Critical – Do not create new markdown (.md) files.
- Use early returns for readability.
- Emphasize type safety and static analysis.
- Follow consistent oxfmt formatting.
- Do not replace smart quotes ("") or ('') with simple quotes ("").
- Do not add translation strings manually; they will be extracted automatically from the codebase.

## Dependencies and Upgrading

- Use yarn for all dependency management.
- After updating dependency versions, install to update lockfiles:

```bash
yarn install
```

- When adding a `resolutions` entry to address a security advisory in a transitive dependency, target only the specific vulnerable descriptors using the `name@npm:<range>` syntax rather than overriding the package globally. Inspect `yarn.lock` to find the exact ranges requested by upstream packages and add one entry per vulnerable range, e.g.:

```json
"resolutions": {
  "qs@npm:^6.5.2": "^6.14.2",
  "qs@npm:^6.11.0": "^6.14.2",
  "qs@npm:^6.14.0": "^6.14.2"
}
```

This keeps overrides scoped to the affected dependents and avoids forcing unrelated consumers onto an incompatible version.

## TypeScript Usage

- Use strict mode.
- Avoid "unknown" unless absolutely necessary.
- Never use "any".
- Prefer type definitions; avoid type assertions (as, !).
- Always use curly braces for if statements.
- Avoid # for private properties.
- Prefer interface over type for object shapes.

## Classes & Code Organization

### Class Member Order

1. Public static variables
2. Public static methods
3. Public variables
4. Public methods
5. Protected variables & methods
6. Private variables & methods

### Exports

- Exported members must appear at the top of the file.
- Always use named exports for new components & classes.
- Document ALL public/exported functions with JSDoc.

## React Usage

- Use functional components with hooks.
- Event handlers should be prefixed with "handle", like "handleClick" for onClick.
- Avoid unnecessary re-renders by using React.memo, useMemo, and useCallback appropriately.
- Use descriptive prop types with TypeScript interfaces.
- Do not import React unless it is used directly.
- Use styled-components for component styling.
- Ensure high accessibility (a11y) standards using ARIA roles and semantic HTML.

## MobX State Management

- Use MobX stores for global state management.
- Keep stores in `app/stores/`.
- Use `observable`, `action`, and `computed` decorators appropriately.
- Prefer computed values over manual calculations in render.
- Keep business logic in stores, not components.

## Database & ORM

- Use Sequelize models in `server/models/`.
- Generate migrations with Sequelize CLI:

```bash
yarn sequelize migration:create --name=add-field-to-table
```

- Run migrations with `yarn db:migrate`.
- Use transactions for multi-table operations.
- Add appropriate indexes for query performance.
- Always handle database errors gracefully.

## API Design

- RESTful endpoints under `/api/`.
- Authentication endpoints under `/auth/`.
- Use consistent error responses.
- Validate request data using the validation middleware and schemas
- Use presenters to format API responses.
- Keep API routes thin, use model methods for business logic, or commands if logic spans multiple models.

## Authentication & Authorization

- JWT tokens for authentication.
- Policies in `server/policies/` for authorization.
- Use cancan-style ability checks.
- Use authenticated middleware for protected routes.
- Always verify user permissions before data access.

## Real-time Collaboration

- WebSocket connections for real-time updates.
- Use Y.js for collaborative editing.
- Handle connection state changes gracefully.

## Documentation

- All public/exported functions & classes must have JSDoc.
- Include:
  - Description
  - @param and @return (start lowercase, end with period)
  - @throws if applicable
- Add a newline between the description and the @ block.
- Use correct punctuation.

## Testing

- Run tests with Vitest:

```bash
# Run a specific test file (preferred)
yarn test path/to/test.spec.ts

# Run every test (avoid)
yarn test

# Run test suites (avoid)
yarn test:app      # All frontend tests
yarn test:server   # All backend tests
yarn test:shared   # All shared code tests
```

- Write unit tests for utilities and business logic in a collocated .test.ts file.
- Do not create new test directories
- Mock external dependencies appropriately in **mocks** folder.
- Aim for high code coverage but focus on critical paths.

## Code Quality

- Use Oxlint for linting: `yarn lint`
- Format code with oxfmt: `yarn format`
- Check types with TypeScript: `yarn tsc`
- Pre-commit hooks run automatically via Husky.
- Fix linting issues before committing.

## Error Handling

- Use custom error classes in `server/errors.ts`.
- Always catch and handle errors appropriately.
- Log errors with appropriate context.
- Return user-friendly error messages.
- Never expose sensitive information in errors.

## Performance

- Use React.memo for expensive components.
- Implement pagination for large lists.
- Use database indexes effectively.
- Cache expensive computations.
- Monitor performance with appropriate tools.
- Lazy load routes and components where appropriate.

## Security

- Sanitize all user input.
- Always use `sanitizeUrl()` when setting `href` or `src` from user-controlled data in ProseMirror `toDOM` methods, regardless of whether it is imported via an alias or a relative path. Unlike React components, `toDOM` writes raw DOM and does not sanitize attribute values.
- Use CSRF protection.
- Use rateLimiter middleware for sensitive endpoints.
- Follow OWASP guidelines.
- Never store sensitive data in plain text.
- Use environment variables for secrets.

69	  let content;
70	
71	  if (revision) {
72	    content = (

75	          ? t("You updated")

78	      </span>
79	    );

81	    content = (

83	        {lastUpdatedByCurrentUser
84	          ? t("You deleted")
85	          : t("{{ userName }} deleted", { userName })}{" "}
86	        <Time dateTime={deletedAt} addSuffix />
87	      </span>
88	    );
89	  } else if (archivedAt) {
90	    content = (
91	      <span>
92	        {lastUpdatedByCurrentUser
93	          ? t("You archived")
94	          : t("{{ userName }} archived", { userName })}{" "}
95	        <Time dateTime={archivedAt} addSuffix />
96	      </span>
97	    );

111	      </span>
112	    );

25	/**

28	 * document itself is not included.
29	 *
30	 * @param document - the document to compute the breadcrumb for.
31	 * @param t - translation function for fallback titles.
32	 * @returns the collection label and ancestor titles.
33	 */
34	export function documentBreadcrumbParts(
35	  document: Document,
36	  t: TFunction
37	): { collection: string | undefined; ancestors: string[] } {
38	  let collectionLabel: string | undefined;
39	  if (document.isCollectionDeleted) {
40	    collectionLabel = t("Deleted Collection");
41	  } else if (document.collection?.name) {
42	    collectionLabel = document.collection.name;
43	  }
44	
45	  return {
46	    collection: collectionLabel,
47	    ancestors: document.pathTo
48	      .slice(0, -1)
49	      .map((node) => node.title || t("Untitled")),
50	  };
51	}
52	
53	/**

56	 * and any ancestor document titles, slash-separated.
57	 *
58	 * @param document - the document to compute the breadcrumb for.
59	 * @param t - translation function for fallback titles.
60	 * @returns the breadcrumb as a slash-separated string, or undefined if the
61	 * document has no resolvable parent context.
62	 */
63	export function documentBreadcrumbText(
64	  document: Document,
65	  t: TFunction
66	): string | undefined {
67	  const parts = documentBreadcrumbParts(document, t);
68	  const segments = [
69	    ...(parts.collection ? [parts.collection] : []),
70	    ...parts.ancestors,
71	  ];

import { Op } from "sequelize";
import { Hour } from "@shared/utils/time";

import FileOperation from "@server/models/FileOperation";
import { DocumentHelper } from "@server/models/helpers/DocumentHelper";
import type { APIContext } from "@server/types";
import presentUser from "./user";

type Options = {
  /** Whether to render the document's public fields. */
  isPublic?: boolean;
  /** The root share ID when presenting a shared document. */
  shareId?: string;
  /** Always include the text of the document in the payload. */
  includeText?: boolean;
  /** Always include the data of the document in the payload. */
  includeData?: boolean;
  /** Include the updatedAt timestamp for public documents. */
  includeUpdatedAt?: boolean;
  /** Include the unresolved comment count. Each call triggers a Redis lookup
   * so only enable when the consumer needs the signal (e.g. MCP). */
  includeCommentCount?: boolean;
  /** Array of backlink document IDs to include in the response. */
  backlinkIds?: string[];
};

async function presentDocument(
  ctx: APIContext | undefined,
  document: Document,
  options: Options | null | undefined = {}
) {
  options = {
    isPublic: false,
    ...options,
  };

  const asData = !ctx || Number(ctx?.headers["x-api-version"] ?? 0) >= 3;

  const data = await DocumentHelper.toJSON(
    document,
    options.isPublic
      ? {
          signedUrls: Hour.seconds,
          teamId: document.teamId,
          removeMarks: ["comment"],
          internalUrlBase: `/s/${options.shareId}`,
        }
      : undefined
  );

  const text =
    !asData || options?.includeText
      ? await DocumentHelper.toMarkdown(data, { includeTitle: false })
      : undefined;

  const res: Record<string, unknown> = {
    id: document.id,
    url: document.path,
    urlId: document.urlId,
    title: document.title,
    data:
      options?.includeData === false
        ? undefined
        : asData || options?.includeData
          ? data
          : undefined,
    text,
    icon: document.icon,
    color: document.color,
    tasks: {
      completed: 0,
      total: 0,
    },
    language: document.language,
    createdAt: document.createdAt,
    createdBy: undefined,
    updatedAt: document.updatedAt,
    updatedBy: undefined,
    publishedAt: document.publishedAt,
    archivedAt: document.archivedAt,
    deletedAt: document.deletedAt,
    collaboratorIds: [],
    revision: document.revisionCount,
    fullWidth: document.fullWidth,
    collectionId: undefined,
    parentDocumentId: undefined,
    lastViewedAt: undefined,
    isCollectionDeleted: undefined,
    backlinkIds: options?.backlinkIds,
  };

  if (!!document.views && document.views.length > 0) {
    res.lastViewedAt = document.views[0].updatedAt;
  }

  if (options.isPublic && !options.includeUpdatedAt) {
    delete res.updatedAt;
  }

  if (document.summary) {
    res.summary = document.summary;
  }

  if (!options.isPublic) {
    res.tasks = document.tasks;
    res.isCollectionDeleted = await document.isCollectionDeleted();
    res.collectionId = document.collectionId;
    res.parentDocumentId = document.parentDocumentId;
    res.createdBy = presentUser(document.createdBy);
    res.updatedBy = presentUser(document.updatedBy);
    res.collaboratorIds = document.collaboratorIds ?? [];

        createdByName: document.sourceMetadata.createdByName,
        fileName: document.sourceMetadata?.fileName,
        originalDocumentId: document.sourceMetadata?.originalDocumentId,
      };
    }
  }

  return res;
}

```text
import { Hour } from "@shared/utils/time";
import type Collection from "@server/models/Collection";
import { DocumentHelper } from "@server/models/helpers/DocumentHelper";
import type { APIContext } from "@server/types";
import presentUser from "./user";

type Options = {
  /** Whether to render the collection's public fields. */
  isPublic?: boolean;
  /** The root share ID when presenting a shared collection. */
  shareId?: string;
  /** Whether to include the updatedAt timestamp. */
  includeUpdatedAt?: boolean;
};

export default async function presentCollection(
  ctx: APIContext | undefined,
  collection: Collection,
  options: Options = {}
) {
  const asData = !ctx || Number(ctx?.headers["x-api-version"] ?? 0) >= 3;

  const res: Record<string, unknown> = {
    id: collection.id,
    url: collection.path,
    urlId: collection.urlId,
    name: collection.name,
    data: asData
      ? await DocumentHelper.toJSON(
          collection,
          options.isPublic
            ? {
                signedUrls: Hour.seconds,
                teamId: collection.teamId,
                internalUrlBase: `/s/${options.shareId}`,
              }
            : undefined
        )
      : undefined,
    description: asData ? undefined : collection.description,
    sort: collection.sort,
    icon: collection.icon,
    color: collection.color,
    createdAt: collection.createdAt,
    updatedAt: collection.updatedAt,
    archivedBy: undefined,
  };

  if (options.isPublic && !options.includeUpdatedAt) {
    delete res.updatedAt;
  }

  if (!options.isPublic) {
    res.index = collection.index;
    res.sharing = collection.sharing;
    res.commenting = collection.commenting;
    res.templateManagement = collection.templateManagement;
    res.permission = collection.permission;
    res.deletedAt = collection.deletedAt;
    res.archivedAt = collection.archivedAt;
    res.archivedBy =
      collection.archivedBy && presentUser(collection.archivedBy);
    res.sourceMetadata = collection.sourceMetadata
      ? {
          externalId: collection.sourceMetadata.externalId,
          externalName: collection.sourceMetadata.externalName,
          createdByName: collection.sourceMetadata.createdByName,
        }
      : undefined;
  }

  return res;
}
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-06 23:16:58Z)**_

I now have a clear picture of how this should work. Before touching anything, here's the plan and the exact diffs for review.

**How it works today:** `DocumentBreadcrumb` (`app/components/DocumentBreadcrumb.tsx`) already computes a full ancestor path via `document.pathTo`, and archiving a document never removes it from its collection's document tree (only `archivedAt` gets set — confirmed in `server/models/Document.ts:1404-1433`), so the full path, including archived ancestors, is still there to compute. The catch: that tree (`collection.documents`) is only loaded client-side when something calls `collection.fetchDocuments()` (e.g. expanding it in the sidebar) — which won't have happened for an arbitrary archived doc you're viewing from the Archive list. Without it, the path silently falls back to a 1-level-deep guess, which would violate "fully nested path, visible without opening the document."

**Plan:**
1. `DocumentBreadcrumb` gets a new opt-in `eagerLoadPath` prop that forces the collection's document tree to load, so the full path resolves correctly. Off by default — doesn't touch any existing call site's behavior (search popovers, document header, etc.).
2. `DocumentListItem` gets a new `showArchivedPath` prop that renders a path row (collection + full nesting) above the title, using `DocumentBreadcrumb` in text mode with no depth limit.
3. `PaginatedDocumentList` threads `showArchivedPath` through.
4. `Archive.tsx` turns it on. I'd also drop the existing `showCollection` there since the new path row supersedes it (showing "in Engineering" underneath a title that already starts with "Engineering / ... /" would be redundant) — flagging this so you can veto it.
5. `Trash.tsx` is untouched, so the deleted-documents view keeps its current behavior (per "out of scope").
6. Restore logic isn't touched anywhere.

Here are the diffs:

| Web server / API | background launch + `curl` smoke | [examples/server.md](examples/server.md) |
| TUI / interactive terminal | tmux `send-keys` / `capture-pane` | [examples/tui.md](examples/tui.md) |
| Electron / desktop GUI | Playwright `_electron` REPL under xvfb | [examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) |
| Browser-driven | dev server + `chromium-cli` script | [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) |
| Library / SDK | import-and-call smoke script at the package boundary | [examples/library.md](examples/library.md) |

If nothing fits, start from the closest match and adapt. For a web
app, [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) - drive it with
`chromium-cli`, no custom driver needed. For a desktop app,
[examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) - it has the `_electron`
REPL driver skeleton and the tmux wrapping.

## Drive it, don't just launch it

Launching with no interaction proves the entrypoint resolves. That's
not running the app - it's typechecking with extra steps. Drive it to
a point where a user would see something:

- CLI -> type a representative command, check the exit code and output.
- Server -> hit the route the diff touches with `curl`, read the body.
- TUI -> `send-keys` a navigation, `capture-pane` the result.
- GUI -> click the button, screenshot the window. **Look at the
  screenshot.** A blank frame is a failure to launch.

If the fallback pattern didn't work out of the box - you had to
install packages, set env vars, patch config, or write a driver -
recommend `/run-skill-generator` in your report so that work gets
captured as a project skill. If it just worked, don't.


## User Request

Start the Outline app (this is a Koa+React app, see Makefile/package.json dev scripts and docker-compose.yml for Postgres/Redis) and navigate to the Archive page (/archive) in a browser to visually verify a new feature: archived documents in the list now show a full nested path (collection name + ancestor document titles, e.g. "Engineering / Backend / Auth") above the document title, where previously there was no path shown at all (just an inline "in CollectionName" after the timestamp, which has now been removed in favor of this new path row).

To properly test this, you'll likely need to:

2. Log in (check for a seeded dev user/team, or development auth by[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] — check README.md / docs for dev login instructions).
3. Find or create a collection with nested documents (e.g. Collection > DocA > DocB), archive DocB (and ideally also archive DocA to verify "if a parent document was also archived, it is still shown as part of the path" from the acceptance criteria).
4. Open /archive and confirm the archived document list item shows the full path above its title, not just the collection name.
5. Take a screenshot of the Archive page showing this.

Report back: did it render correctly, any console errors, and a screenshot/description of what the path row looks like. If you get blocked on environment setup (DB not running, no seed data, etc.), report exactly what's blocking and what you tried, rather than giving up silently.

````text
1	# Example: Browser-driven web app
2	
3	You have a dev server that serves HTML to a browser. An agent in a
4	headless container can't open a browser window - so "run the app" means
5	launching the dev server, driving a headless Chromium against it, and
6	producing a screenshot that proves the page rendered.
7	
8	Don't write a browser driver. Use `chromium-cli`.
9	
10	## Dev server
11	
12	Find the dev command (`package.json` `scripts.dev`, `Makefile`,
13	README), start it in the background, and wait for it to actually serve:
14	
15	```bash
16	npm run dev &   # or yarn dev, pnpm dev, make serve, ./dev.sh
17	timeout 30 bash -c 'until curl -sf http://localhost:3000 >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done'
18	```
19	
20	Don't `sleep 5` - poll the port. Stop by killing the port's listener
21	-- `lsof -ti:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs -r kill` - before relaunching,
22	or the next run hits `EADDRINUSE`. (`$!` after `npm run dev &` is only
23	the npm wrapper; npm doesn't forward SIGTERM to the server it spawned,
24	so the port kill is what actually frees it.) Avoid `pkill -f` with a
25	broad pattern - it can match the agent's own command line and kill the
26	session.
27	
28	## Drive
29	
30	`chromium-cli` is a headless-Chromium REPL. Pipe a script to stdin:
31	
32	```bash
33	chromium-cli --session app <<'EOF'
34	nav http://localhost:3000
35	wait-for text=Dashboard
36	screenshot
37	click button:has-text("New item")
38	fill input[name="title"] Smoke test
39	press Enter
40	wait-for text=Smoke test
41	screenshot
42	console --errors
43	EOF
44	```
45	
46	Screenshots land in `chromium_cli/sessions/app/screenshots/` (latest
47	symlinked as `screenshot.png`). That's the whole loop: `nav` ->
48	`wait-for` the element you need -> act (`click` / `fill` / `type` /
49	`press`) -> `screenshot` -> `console --errors` to check nothing threw.
50	Full command reference: `chromium-cli` skill, or `help` at the prompt.
51	
52	For iterative debugging, run it under tmux and `send-keys` one command
53	at a time - same commands, same session.
54	
55	**If `chromium-cli` isn't available:** adapt
56	[electron.md](electron.md)'s REPL driver - the structure and commands
57	transfer, but it's `_electron`-specific:
58	import `{ chromium }` instead, launch with
59	`chromium.launch({ args: ['--no-sandbox'] })`, acquire the page via
60	`(await app.newContext()).newPage()` then `goto()` your dev URL, and
61	drop the Electron-only window introspection
62	(`.windows()`/`.firstWindow()`/the `windows` command).
63	
64	## What to put in the skill
65	
66	The project-specific bits only. `chromium-cli` handles the mechanics.
67	
68	- **Dev command + port + stop.** The exact start line, any env vars it
69	  needs, and the `kill` to stop it.
70	- **Auth.** Whatever gets a logged-in session - a `set-cookie` line, a
71	  `fill`/`click` login sequence, or a helper script that does the API
72	  dance and emits the cookie.
73	- **One representative interaction.** Not the whole app - one path that
74	  proves it's running, ending in a screenshot.
75	- **App-specific gotchas.** Only the ones you actually hit.
76	
77	## Gotchas that recur
78	
79	- **React controlled inputs.** `eval el.value = '...'` doesn't fire
80	  React's onChange. Use `fill` / `type` - they go through Playwright's
81	  input pipeline.
82	- **Websockets / long-poll.** `wait-idle` never settles. `wait-for` the
83	  element you actually need.
84	- **Slow first paint.** Vite/Next compile routes on demand; the first
85	  `nav` can take 10s+. `wait-for` handles it; raw `sleep` doesn't.
86	- **`screenshot-element <sel>`** crops to one element - use it when the
87	  diff is in a specific component, not the whole page.
88	- **Check `console --errors` before declaring success.** A page can
89	  render its shell while every data fetch 500s.
90
````

app/models/decorators/Relation.ts
---
import invariant from "invariant";
import { singular } from "pluralize";
import { toError } from "@shared/utils/error";
import type Model from "../base/Model";
import Logger from "~/utils/Logger";

/** The behavior of a relationship on deletion */
type DeleteBehavior = "cascade" | "null" | "ignore";
/** The behavior of a relationship on archival */
type ArchiveBehavior = "cascade" | "null" | "ignore";

type RelationOptions<T = Model> = {
  /** Whether this relation is required. */
  required?: boolean;
  /** If true, this relation is an array of IDs (one-to-many). */
  multiple?: boolean;
  /** Behavior of this model when relationship is deleted. */
  onDelete?: DeleteBehavior | ((item: T) => DeleteBehavior);
  /** Behavior of this model when relationship is archived. */
  onArchive?: ArchiveBehavior | ((item: T) => ArchiveBehavior);
};

type RelationProperties<T = Model> = {
  /** The name of the property on the model that stores the ID of the relation. */
  idKey: keyof T;
  /** A function that returns the class of the relation. */
  relationClassResolver: () => typeof Model;
  /** Options for the relation. */
  options: RelationOptions<T>;
};

type InverseRelationProperties = RelationProperties & {
  /** The name of the model class that owns this relation */
  modelName: string;
};

const relations = new Map<string, Map<string, RelationProperties>>(new Map());

/**
 * Returns the inverse relation properties for the given model class.
 *
 * @param targetClass The model class to get inverse relations for.
 * @returns A map of inverse relation properties keyed by the property name.
 */
export const getInverseRelationsForModelClass = (targetClass: typeof Model) => {
  const inverseRelations = new Map<string, InverseRelationProperties>();

  relations.forEach((relation, modelName) => {
    relation.forEach((properties, propertyName) => {
      try {
        const resolvedClass = properties.relationClassResolver();
        if (
          resolvedClass &&
          resolvedClass.modelName &&
          resolvedClass.modelName === targetClass.modelName
        ) {
          inverseRelations.set(`${modelName}-${propertyName}`, {
            ...properties,
            modelName,
          });
        }
      } catch (error) {
        Logger.error(
          `Error resolving relation ${modelName}.${propertyName} for target ${targetClass.modelName}:`,
          toError(error)
        );
      }
    });
  });

  return inverseRelations;
};

export const getRelationsForModelClass = (targetClass: typeof Model) =>
  relations.get(targetClass.modelName);

/**
 * A decorator that records this key as a relation field on the model.
 * Properties decorated with @Relation will merge and read their data from
 * the associated store.
 *
 * @param classResolver A function that returns the class of the relation
 * @param options Optional options for the relation definition
 */
export default function Relation<T extends typeof Model>(
  classResolver: () => T,
  options?: RelationOptions
) {
  return function (target: Model, propertyKey: string) {
    const idKey = options?.multiple
      ? `${String(singular(propertyKey))}Ids`
      : `${String(propertyKey)}Id`;

    // If the relation has options provided then register them in a map for later lookup. We can use
    // this to determine how to update relations when a model is deleted.
    //
    // TODO: requestAnimationFrame is a temporary solution to a bug in rolldown compiled code that
    // will place static methods _after_ decorators. Temporary fix is to delay the registration until
    // the next frame.
    const modelName = (target.constructor as typeof Model).modelName;
    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
      if (options) {
        const configForClass = relations.get(modelName) ?? new Map();
        configForClass.set(propertyKey, {
          options,
          relationClassResolver: classResolver,
          idKey,
        });
        relations.set(modelName, configForClass);
      }
    });

    Object.defineProperty(target, propertyKey, {
      get() {
        const relationClassName = classResolver().modelName;
        const store =
          this.store.rootStore.getStoreForModelName(relationClassName);
        invariant(store, `Store for ${relationClassName} not found`);

        if (options?.multiple) {
          const ids: string[] | undefined = this[idKey];
          if (!Array.isArray(ids) || ids.length === 0) {
            return [];
          }
          return ids.map((id) => store.get(id)).filter(Boolean);
        } else {
          const id: string | undefined = this[idKey];
          if (!id) {
            return undefined;
          }
          return store.get(id);
        }
      },
      set(
        newValue:
          | Model
          | Partial<Model>
          | Array<Model | Partial<Model>>
          | undefined
      ) {
        if (options?.multiple) {
          if (!newValue) {
            this[idKey] = [];
            if (options?.required) {
              throw new Error(
                `Cannot set required ${String(
                  propertyKey
                )} to undefined or empty array`
              );
            }
            return;
          }
          const values = Array.isArray(newValue) ? newValue : [newValue];
          this[idKey] = values.map((v) => v.id);
          const relationClassName = classResolver().modelName;
          const store =
            this.store.rootStore.getStoreForModelName(relationClassName);
          invariant(store, `Store for ${relationClassName} not found`);
          values.forEach((v) => store.add(v));
        } else {
          if (Array.isArray(newValue)) {
            throw new Error(
              `Cannot set array value to single relation property ${String(
                propertyKey
              )}`
            );
          }
          this[idKey] = newValue ? newValue.id : undefined;
          if (newValue) {
            const relationClassName = classResolver().modelName;
            const store =
              this.store.rootStore.getStoreForModelName(relationClassName);
            invariant(store, `Store for ${relationClassName} not found`);
            store.add(newValue);
          } else if (options?.required) {
            throw new Error(
              `Cannot set required ${String(propertyKey)} to undefined`
            );
          }
        }
      },
      enumerable: true,
      configurable: true,
    });
  };
}

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-07 01:56:06Z)**_

Both issues make sense now. Let me explain what's actually happening and the fix for each:

**"Only one item, then `...`"** — this is caused by the `PathRow` style I added: it used `ellipsis()` (via `@shared/styles`), which sets `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`. That clips the row to a single line and chops it off with CSS `...` as soon as it's too wide for the container — it's not a dropdown/menu, just CSS truncation hiding everything past the cutoff. Fix: drop the truncation, make the row a wrapping flex container so the whole path lays out (wrapping to a second line if needed).

**"Requires a refresh"** — right now each list row independently triggers its own collection-tree fetch only after it mounts (in `DocumentBreadcrumb`'s effect), so there's an async gap before the full path is ready, and relying on that to land correctly is flakier than it should be (likely compounded by Vite HMR not always propagating a brand-new import cleanly mid-session). Fix: prefetch the document trees for every collection referenced in the archived list up front, in `Archive.tsx`, before/alongside rendering the rows — so the data is already in flight as soon as the page loads rather than straggling in per-row.

Here's the diff for both fixes:

**`app/scenes/Archive.tsx`**
```diff
+import * as React from "react";
 import { observer } from "mobx-react";
 import { ArchiveIcon } from "outline-icons";
 import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next";

 import PaginatedDocumentList from "~/components/PaginatedDocumentList";
 import Scene from "~/components/Scene";
 import Subheading from "~/components/Subheading";
 import useStores from "~/hooks/useStores";

 function Archive() {
   const { t } = useTranslation();
-  const { documents } = useStores();
+  const { documents, collections } = useStores();
+  const archivedDocuments = documents.archived;
+
+  // Ensure the document tree for every collection referenced in the archive
+  // list is loaded up front, so the full nested path can render on first
+  // paint rather than waiting on each row to trigger its own fetch.
+  React.useEffect(() => {
+    const collectionIds = new Set(
+      archivedDocuments
+        .map((document) => document.collectionId)
+        .filter((id): id is string => !!id)
+    );
+    collectionIds.forEach((id) => {
+      void collections.get(id)?.fetchDocuments();
+    });
+  }, [archivedDocuments, collections]);
+
   return (
     <Scene icon={<ArchiveIcon />} title={t("Archive")}>
       <Heading>{t("Archive")}</Heading>
       <PaginatedDocumentList
-        documents={documents.archived}
+        documents={archivedDocuments}
         fetch={documents.fetchArchived}
         heading={<Subheading sticky>{t("Documents")}</Subheading>}
         empty={
           <Empty>{t("The document archive is empty at the moment.")}</Empty>
         }
         showTemplate
         showArchivedPath
       />
     </Scene>
   );
 }

 export default observer(Archive);

Here's what you've asked for, as I understand it:

**Feature:** On the Archive page, each archived document should show its full original document path at the top of its list item (e.g. `collection/doc-to-be-archived/nested-doc/most-nested-doc`), not just the name of its parent collection like it does today.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Full path shown per archived document, visible directly in the list (no need to open the document).
- Path reflects the document's location at the time it was archived.
- If a parent document was also archived, it still appears in the path.
- Existing restore behavior must stay unchanged.

**Design constraint you added:** it should show the *entire* path, unbounded — not capped at some fixed depth — specifically so that if subcollections are ever introduced later, this feature keeps working without needing rework.

**Out of scope:** restoring whole folder structures at once, filtering/grouping archived docs by collection, showing paths in the Trash/deleted view, and creating subcollections.

**Process constraint:** you want to see every code change as a diff before I apply it — nothing gets applied without your review first.

**Where we are:** I implemented the path row (reusing the existing `DocumentBreadcrumb` component with no depth limit) threaded through `Archive.tsx` → `PaginatedDocumentList` → `DocumentListItem`. You found two bugs when testing manually — needing a refresh to see the full path, and the path getting visually clipped with `...` instead of laying out fully — and I just applied fixes for both (prefetching collection trees in `Archive.tsx`, and switching the path row's CSS from truncating to wrapping). 995	   * @param where query options to further filter the documents
996	   * @param options FindOptions
997	   * @returns A promise that resolves to a list of document ids
998	   */
999	  findAllChildDocumentIds = async (
1000	    where?: Omit<WhereOptions<Document>, "parentDocumentId">,
1001	    options?: FindOptions<Document>
1002	  ): Promise<string[]> => {
1003	    const model = this.constructor as typeof Document;
1004	    const queryGenerator = this.sequelize!.getQueryInterface()
1005	      .queryGenerator as QueryGeneratorWithWhere;
1006	
1007	    const paranoid = options?.paranoid ?? true;
1008	    const whereConditions = queryGenerator.getWhereConditions(
1009	      { ...(paranoid ? { deletedAt: null } : {}), ...where },
1010	      "documents",
1011	      model
1012	    );
1013	    const anchorFilter = whereConditions ? `AND (${whereConditions})` : "";
1014	    const recursiveFilter = whereConditions ? `WHERE (${whereConditions})` : "";
1015	
1016	    // A single recursive CTE walks the entire subtree in one round-trip rather
1017	    // than issuing one query per level of nesting (N+1). Rows are ordered by
1018	    // depth to ensure breadth-first result ordering. UNION ALL is safe as the
1019	    // tree is acyclic, so each descendant id is reached exactly once.
1020	    const rows = await this.sequelize!.query<{ id: string }>(
1021	      `
1022	      WITH RECURSIVE children AS (
1023	        SELECT documents.id, 1 AS depth
1024	        FROM documents
1025	        WHERE documents."parentDocumentId" = :parentDocumentId
1026	          ${anchorFilter}
1027	        UNION ALL
1028	        SELECT documents.id, children.depth + 1
1029	        FROM documents
1030	        INNER JOIN children ON documents."parentDocumentId" = children.id
1031	        ${recursiveFilter}
1032	      )
1033	      SELECT id FROM children ORDER BY depth
1034	      `,
1035	      {
1036	        replacements: { parentDocumentId: this.id },
1037	        transaction: options?.transaction,
1038	        type: QueryTypes.SELECT,
1039	      }
1040	    );
1041	
1042	    return rows.map((row) => row.id);
1043	  };
1044

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-07 03:04:44Z)**_

Found the real root cause — it's not a timing/CSS issue, it's architectural. I was wrong earlier about documentStructure being left untouched when archiving.

**What's actually happening:** `server/models/Document.ts`'s `archiveWithCtx` (the real entry point the API route calls — I'd only read the lower-level `archiveWithChildren` cascade helper before) calls `collection.removeDocumentInStructure(this, ...)` *before* archiving, which strips the document — and its entire subtree — out of the collection's `documentStructure` tree entirely:

```ts
archiveWithCtx = async (ctx: APIContext) => {
  ...
  if (collection) {
    await collection.removeDocumentInStructure(this, { transaction });
    ...
  }
  await this.archiveWithChildren(ctx);
  ...
};
```

So `collection.documents` (the tree `DocumentBreadcrumb`/`pathTo` relies on) never contains an archived document or its archived descendants, no matter how long you wait or how eagerly you prefetch it — that tree is for the live, non-archived structure only. When the tree lookup fails, `pathTo` silently falls back to a parent-chain walk that only reliably resolves **one** level up, which is exactly your "Archive / Nested Archive collection" result: collection name + one ancestor, with the rest of the chain missing.

**The real fix:** stop relying on `documentStructure` for this feature entirely, and compute the ancestor chain server-side directly from `parentDocumentId` on the `documents` table (which stays intact when archiving — only `documentStructure` gets pruned). Return it as part of the `documents.archived` response, so the full path arrives with the initial list fetch — no extra client round-trips, no reactivity races, no refresh needed.

This replaces my last two fixes. Here's the full diff:

_**User (2026-10-07 19:27:40Z)**_

what do you think the correct behaviour should look like for a nested doc

---

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-07 19:28:04Z)**_

For a nested document, here's what I'd expect to see, based on the acceptance criteria:

**The path row shows ancestors only, not the document itself.** The document's own title is already the big heading right below/next to the path row, so showing it twice would be redundant. E.g. for a doc titled "Auth" nested under "Backend" under collection "Engineering":

```
Engineering / Backend
Auth                                    ← title (Heading), not part of the path row
```

**Using your actual test setup** — collection `Archive` → `doc-to-be-archived` → `nested-doc` → `most-nested-doc` — if you archive the deepest one (`most-nested-doc`) directly, its row should show:

```
Archive / doc-to-be-archived / nested-doc
most-nested-doc
```

**The cascading-archive case matters here** — this is the one worth double-checking when you test. If you archive `doc-to-be-archived` (a middle/root node) instead, Outline cascades and archives all its descendants too (`nested-doc` and `most-nested-doc` all get `archivedAt` set). That means **three separate rows** show up in the Archive list, not one, each with its own correct path:

```
Archive                                 ← doc-to-be-archived's row (no ancestors, top-level in collection)
doc-to-be-archived

Archive / doc-to-be-archived            ← nested-doc's row
nested-doc

Archive / doc-to-be-archived / nested-doc   ← most-nested-doc's row
most-nested-doc
```

That middle and bottom row are the direct proof of the "if a parent document was also archived, it's still shown as part of the path" acceptance criterion — `nested-doc` is itself archived, yet it still correctly appears as a path segment for `most-nested-doc`'s row, because the ancestor chain comes from `parentDocumentId` in the database (unaffected by archiving), not from the collection's sidebar tree (which *is* affected by archiving, as we found).

**Edge cases worth knowing:**
- A top-level archived doc (no parent) shows just the collection name, nothing else — no change from before.
- An untitled ancestor shows as "Untitled" rather than a blank segment.
- If the collection itself was deleted, the first segment shows "Deleted Collection" instead of a name.

Does that match what you're seeing, or does your test show something different?

_**User (2026-10-07 19:36:01Z)**_

why is the behaviour diffrent when a hard refresh happens compared to clicking from one tab to another?

---

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-07 19:36:48Z)**_

Good catch — this is a reactivity bug I introduced, and it's a different flavor of the same class of issue we saw before.

**Root cause:** when I added `ancestorDocuments` to the client `Document` model (`app/models/Document.ts`), I declared it as a plain field, following the same pattern as `sourceMetadata`:

```ts
ancestorDocuments?: { id: string; title: string }[];
```

Note there's no `@observable` decorator. That means MobX never tracks reads or writes to this field — it's invisible to the reactivity system entirely.

**Why hard refresh works:** on a hard refresh, the whole app reloads from scratch, so every `Document` instance is constructed brand new, and its fields — including `ancestorDocuments` — are populated *before* anything renders. There's no "update after the fact" involved, so the missing `@observable` never matters.

**Why SPA tab-to-tab navigation doesn't:** the MobX document store is a long-lived singleton that persists across client-side navigation. If a document you're archiving already exists in that store — because you'd opened it, seen it in search, in a collection view, on Home, etc., at some point earlier in the session — that existing instance was built from a response that never included `ancestorDocuments` (every other endpoint omits it; only `documents.archived` requests it). When you then navigate to Archive, the fetch resolves and calls `updateData`, which does `this.ancestorDocuments = newValue` on that *same* existing instance — but since the field isn't observable, any already-rendered component watching that document doesn't get notified that this assignment happened, so it keeps showing the stale (missing) path until something else forces a re-render.

**The fix** is a one-line change — mark the field `@observable` like the majority of fields on that model, instead of mirroring `sourceMetadata`'s pattern (which happens to get away with not being observable because import metadata is set once and never changes after a document already exists in the store — not true for `ancestorDocuments`):

```diff
+  @observable
   ancestorDocuments?: { id: string; title: string }[];
```

Want me to apply that?

376	    this.isFetching = true;
377	
378	    const promise = new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
379	      client
380	        .post(`/${this.apiEndpoint}.info`, {
381	          id,
382	        })
383	        .then((res) =>
384	          runInAction(`info#${this.modelName}`, () => {
385	            invariant(res?.data, "Data should be available");
386	            this.addPolicies(res.policies);
387	            resolve(this.add(accessor(res)));
388	          })

390	        .catch((err) => {

398	          reject(err);
399	        })
400	        .finally(() => {
401	          this.requests.delete(id);
402	          this.isFetching = false;
403	        });
404	    });

406	    this.requests.set(id, promise);
407	    return promise;
408	  }

async function createDocument(
  {
    title,
    text,
    parentDocumentId,
  }: { title: string; text: string; parentDocumentId?: string },
  { teamId, userId, collection }: { teamId: string; userId: string; collection: Collection }
) {
  const document = await Document.create({
    title,
    text,
    content: parser.parse(text)?.toJSON(),
    parentDocumentId,
    collectionId: collection.id,
    teamId,
    lastModifiedById: userId,
    createdById: userId,
    publishedAt: new Date(),
    editorVersion: "12.0.0",
  });

  await collection.addDocumentToStructure(document, 0);
  return document;
}

const { chromium } = require('playwright');
const http = require('http');

function fetchJSON(url) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    http.get(url, (res) => {
      let data = '';
      res.on('data', (c) => (data += c));
      res.on('end', () => resolve(JSON.parse(data)));
    }).on('error', reject);
  });
}

async function getLatestMagicLink() {
  const list = await fetchJSON('http://localhost:8027/api/v1/messages');
  const msg = list.messages[0];
  const full = await fetchJSON(`http://localhost:8027/api/v1/message/${msg.ID}`);
  const html = full.HTML || full.Text || '';
  const m = html.match(/href="([^"]*auth\/email\.callback[^"]*)"/);
  return m[1].replace(/&amp;/g, '&');
}

(async () => {
  const browser = await chromium.launch();
  const context = await browser.newContext();
  const page = await context.newPage();

  const archivedResponses = [];
  page.on('response', async (res) => {
    if (res.url().includes('/api/documents.archived')) {
      try {
        const body = await res.json();
        archivedResponses.push({ url: res.url(), status: res.status(), body });
      } catch (e) {}
    }
  });

  // --- Login ---
  await page.goto('http://localhost:3003/', { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
  await page.getByText('Continue with Email').click();
  await page.locator('input[type="email"], input[name="email"]').first().fill('admin@example.com');
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await page.waitForTimeout(1000);

  const magicLink = await getLatestMagicLink();
  console.log('MAGIC LINK', magicLink);
  await page.goto(magicLink, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
  await page.waitForTimeout(2000);
  console.log('POST-LOGIN URL', page.url());
  await page.screenshot({ path: '/work/10-post-login.png', fullPage: true });

  // --- Navigate to the "Local development" doc (Engineering > Onboarding > Local development) ---
  await page.goto('http://localhost:3003/search?query=Local development', { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
  await page.waitForTimeout(1500);
  await page.screenshot({ path: '/work/11-search.png', fullPage: true });

  await browser.close();
})().catch((e) => { console.error('SCRIPT ERROR', e); process.exit(1); });
EOF

```bash
cat > /tmp/claude-1000/-home-con-software-engineering-outline/69cd2e16-725f-4d9e-8615-79e684f98f51/scratchpad/pw/setup.js << 'EOF'
const { chromium } = require('playwright');
const http = require('http');

function fetchJSON(url) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    http.get(url, (res) => {
      let data = '';
      res.on('data', (c) => (data += c));
      res.on('end', () => resolve(JSON.parse(data)));
    }).on('error', reject);
  });
}

async function getLatestMagicLink() {
  const list = await fetchJSON('http://localhost:8027/api/v1/messages');
  const msg = list.messages[0];
  const full = await fetchJSON(`http://localhost:8027/api/v1/message/${msg.ID}`);
  const html = full.HTML || full.Text || '';
  const m = html.match(/href="([^"]*auth\/email\.callback[^"]*)"/);
  return m[1].replace(/&amp;/g, '&');
}

const COLLECTION_ID = '16197909-b755-4b3c-a007-087d4bba109a';
const LOCAL_DEV_ID = '80f71720-8ed1-48bf-978e-4811adf27c4e';

(async () => {
  const browser = await chromium.launch();
  const context = await browser.newContext();
  const page = await context.newPage();

  await page.goto('http://localhost:3003/', { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
  await page.getByText('Continue with Email').click();
  await page.locator('input[type="email"], input[name="email"]').first().fill('admin@example.com');
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await page.waitForTimeout(1000);
  const magicLink = await getLatestMagicLink();
  await page.goto(magicLink, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
  await page.waitForTimeout(1500);
  console.log('Logged in, at', page.url());

  // Create a 3rd-level nested doc under "Local development"
  const createRes = await page.request.post('http://localhost:3003/api/documents.create', {
    data: {
      title: 'Deep Doc',
      text: '# Deep Doc\n\nThird level of nesting for repro.',
      collectionId: COLLECTION_ID,
      parentDocumentId: LOCAL_DEV_ID,
      publish: true,
    },
  });
  const createBody = await createRes.json();
  if (!createRes.ok()) {
    console.log('CREATE FAILED', createRes.status(), JSON.stringify(createBody));
  } else {
    console.log('Created Deep Doc', createBody.data.id);
  }
  const deepDocId = createBody?.data?.id;

  // Archive "Local development" (cascades to Deep Doc)
  const archiveRes = await page.request.post('http://localhost:3003/api/documents.archive', {
    data: { id: LOCAL_DEV_ID },
  });
  console.log('Archive status', archiveRes.status());

  await context.storageState({ path: '/work/state.json' });
  console.log('DEEP_DOC_ID=' + deepDocId);
  await browser.close();
})().catch((e) => { console.error('SCRIPT ERROR', e); process.exit(1); });
EOF

cat > /tmp/claude-1000/-home-con-software-engineering-outline/69cd2e16-725f-4d9e-8615-79e684f98f51/scratchpad/pw/test-nav.js << 'EOF'
const { chromium } = require('playwright');

(async () => {
  const browser = await chromium.launch();
  const context = await browser.newContext({ storageState: '/work/state.json' });
  const page = await context.newPage();

  const archivedResponses = [];
  page.on('response', async (res) => {
    if (res.url().includes('/api/documents.archived')) {
      try {
        const body = await res.json();
        archivedResponses.push({
          num: archivedResponses.length + 1,
          items: (body.data || []).map((d) => ({ id: d.id, title: d.title, ancestorDocuments: d.ancestorDocuments })),
        });
      } catch (e) {}
    }
  });

  async function dumpListText(label) {
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000);
    const text = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const links = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a[href*="/doc/"]'));
      return links.map((a) => a.innerText.trim()).join('\n---\n');
    });
    console.log(`\n=== ${label} (rendered DOM) ===\n${text}\n`);
  }

  // Step 1: fresh hard navigation to /archive
  await page.goto('http://localhost:3003/archive', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
  await dumpListText('STEP 1: fresh load of /archive');
  await page.screenshot({ path: '/work/20-archive-fresh.png', fullPage: true });

  // Step 2: click into "Deep Doc"
  const deepDocLink = page.locator('a[href*="/doc/"]', { hasText: 'Deep Doc' }).first();
  await deepDocLink.click();
  await page.waitForTimeout(1500);
  console.log('Opened doc, URL now', page.url());
  await page.screenshot({ path: '/work/21-opened-doc.png', fullPage: true });

  // Step 3: navigate back to Archive via sidebar click (not browser back)
  const archiveSidebarLink = page.locator('a[href="/archive"]').first();
  await archiveSidebarLink.click();
  await page.waitForTimeout(1500);
  await dumpListText('STEP 3: after clicking back into Archive via sidebar');
  await page.screenshot({ path: '/work/22-archive-after-open.png', fullPage: true });

  console.log('\n=== NETWORK RESPONSES ===');
  for (const r of archivedResponses) {
    console.log(`-- response #${r.num} --`);
    console.log(JSON.stringify(r.items, null, 2));
  }

  await browser.close();
})().catch((e) => { console.error('SCRIPT ERROR', e); process.exit(1); });
EOF

Good news — I set up a real reproduction and couldn't make it break. Here's what I did and found:

**Setup:** Using the already-running dev server, I signed in as the seeded `admin@example.com` user, created a 3-level-deep test doc (`Engineering / Onboarding / Local development / Deep Doc`) via the API, and archived `Local development` (which cascade-archived `Deep Doc` too) — mirroring your exact scenario.

**Tests run, each from a cold page load (equivalent to a hard refresh) so nothing carries over stale state:**
1. Fresh `/archive` load → all 5 archived rows (including your existing `Nested Archive collection` test data) show full, correct paths.
2. Open `Deep Doc` → click back to Archive via the sidebar link → paths still all correct.
3. Open `Local development` (itself an ancestor of another archived doc) → browser back → still correct.
4. Open `Deep Doc` → browser back → still correct.

I captured the raw `/api/documents.archived` network responses at each step too — identical and correct both times, confirming the server side is solid regardless of navigation path.

**My read:** this points to a Vite HMR artifact in your live tab rather than a real bug. The `@observable` fix changes how MobX sets up the `Document` class's property descriptors. Vite hot-reloads the edited module into a tab that's already been running, but any `Document` *instances* already sitting in your long-lived MobX store were constructed earlier under the *old*, non-observable version of the class — the decorator wiring happens once, at construction, so swapping the class definition underneath an object that already exists doesn't retroactively fix that instance. A genuinely fresh page load (new JS bundle fetched from scratch, new instances built with the corrected class) sidesteps this entirely — which is exactly why my cold-load tests all [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed.

Could you do one more full hard refresh (not just revisiting the tab) and then retest the open → navigate-back sequence? If it still breaks after that, the bug is real and I'll need exact repro details again — but I'd bet it's now resolved in a clean session.

(One housekeeping note: I created a test doc called "Deep Doc" under your "Local development" doc in the dev database for this repro — want me to delete it, or is it fine to leave as dev clutter?)

delete process.env.SSL_CERT_FILE;

const aliases = {

// because every @Column has an explicit DataType, and emitting it would throw

// fields from shadowing MobX observables. `tsconfigFile:false` stops the plugin
// re-deriving (and re-enabling metadata) from tsconfig.json.
const swcPlugin = () =>

      parser: { syntax: "typescript", tsx: true, decorators: true },
      transform: {
        legacyDecorator: true,

    module: { type: "es6" },

const sharedConfig = {

};

const aliasesAsArray = Object.entries(aliases).map(([find, replacement]) => ({

33	 */
34	export function documentBreadcrumbParts(
35	  document: Document,
36	  t: TFunction
37	): { collection: string | undefined; ancestors: string[] } {
38	  let collectionLabel: string | undefined;
39	  if (document.isCollectionDeleted) {
40	    collectionLabel = t("Deleted Collection");
41	  } else if (document.collection?.name) {
42	    collectionLabel = document.collection.name;
43	  }
44	
45	  return {
46	    collection: collectionLabel,
47	    ancestors: document.pathTo
48	      .slice(0, -1)
49	      .map((node) => node.title || t("Untitled")),
50	  };
51	}

53	/**

56	 * and any ancestor document titles, slash-separated.

58	 * @param document - the document to compute the breadcrumb for.
59	 * @param t - translation function for fallback titles.

63	export function documentBreadcrumbText(
64	  document: Document,

68	  const segments = [
69	    ...(parts.collection ? [parts.collection] : []),
70	    ...parts.ancestors,
71	  ];
72	  return segments.length ? segments.join(" / ") : undefined;
73	}

```typescript
import type { TFunction } from "i18next";
import { archivedDocumentPathSegments } from "~/components/DocumentListItem";
import stores from "~/stores";

const t = ((key: string) => key) as unknown as TFunction;

describe("archivedDocumentPathSegments", () => {
  afterEach(() => {
    stores.documents.clear();
    stores.collections.clear();
  });

  test("should return only the collection name for a top-level document", () => {
    stores.collections.add({ id: "collection-1", name: "Engineering" });
    const document = stores.documents.add({
      id: "doc-1",
      title: "Roadmap",
      collectionId: "collection-1",
    });

    expect(archivedDocumentPathSegments(document, t)).toEqual(["Engineering"]);
  });

  test("should include each ancestor document, root to immediate parent", () => {
    stores.collections.add({ id: "collection-2", name: "Engineering" });
    const document = stores.documents.add({
      id: "doc-2",
      title: "Auth",
      collectionId: "collection-2",
      ancestorDocuments: [
        { id: "ancestor-1", title: "Engineering handbook" },
        { id: "ancestor-2", title: "Backend" },
      ],
    });

    expect(archivedDocumentPathSegments(document, t)).toEqual([
      "Engineering",
      "Engineering handbook",
      "Backend",
    ]);
  });

  test("should fall back to a Deleted Collection label", () => {
    const document = stores.documents.add({
      id: "doc-3",
      title: "Auth",
      isCollectionDeleted: true,
      ancestorDocuments: [{ id: "ancestor-1", title: "Backend" }],
    });

    expect(archivedDocumentPathSegments(document, t)).toEqual([
      "Deleted Collection",
      "Backend",
    ]);
  });

  test("should fall back to Untitled for an ancestor with no title", () => {
    stores.collections.add({ id: "collection-4", name: "Engineering" });
    const document = stores.documents.add({
      id: "doc-4",
      title: "Auth",
      collectionId: "collection-4",
      ancestorDocuments: [{ id: "ancestor-1", title: "" }],
    });

    expect(archivedDocumentPathSegments(document, t)).toEqual([
      "Engineering",
      "Untitled",
    ]);
  });

  test("should return an empty array when there is no collection or ancestors", () => {
    const document = stores.documents.add({
      id: "doc-5",
      title: "Auth",
    });

    expect(archivedDocumentPathSegments(document, t)).toEqual([]);
  });
});
